journal_of_m_cov_o4_o5o4 ATOM:DFTo5 ATOM:DFTshared claim n93 values each — equal-length proxy
The covariation generator has no panel_conditions field to read. A sample series is detected from the observation text — three or more numbers in one sweep — and two series pair when they are the same length. Length is not comparability, which is why 37% of sampled covariation propositions set quantities of different kinds against each other.

1 pair(s) found at the pair stage did not become items: a spine edge whose two claims share one evidence node is not a pair, and ten such self-pairs were dropped across the corpus.

key — the combining proposition
Putting resistivity and power factor together shows the two trends move consistently in the direction expected if PF is driven by the resistivity change: the composition with the lowest resistivity (x=0.01, ~12-23 micro-ohm m at 300 K) is also the composition with the highest power factor (~29 at 300 K), while x=0, which has by far the highest resistivity (~650), has the lowest power factor (at most ~5). Likewise, for doped samples resistivity rises with T while the x=0.01 power factor falls from ~29 at 300 K to ~22 at 623 K, again consistent with PF tracking the inverse of resistivity as T increases.
limits
  • This is a co-variation across composition and two temperatures, not a demonstrated mechanism: no Seebeck-coefficient values are given in either observation, and power factor is a composite quantity (Seebeck squared over resistivity) so the resistivity trend alone cannot account for the full power-factor trend
  • The x=0 case breaks the simple picture: its resistivity falls with T (unlike doped samples, whose resistivity rises with T) yet its power factor stays low throughout, showing something besides resistivity (i.e. Seebeck coefficient) must also be governing the power factor there
  • Only two temperatures (300 K and 623 K) are given for the power-factor comparison, which is enough to support an ordering/direction but not a continuous temperature relationship
  • The pairing shows association/consistency between the two panels, not that resistivity alone causes the power-factor level or ranking
not identifiableWhether the power-factor trend (highest at x=0.01, low at x=0) is driven by the resistivity change versus by an unreported Seebeck-coefficient change cannot be separated from these two observations alone

key — the combining proposition
Together, the DFT band structure (Se doping pulling the M, K, L conduction-band minima from ~0.15 eV above E_F down to E_F while the Gamma minimum stays ~0.35-0.4 eV up) gives a plausible electronic-structure mechanism -- multi-valley convergence at E_F -- for why doped samples show much higher power factor than the undoped sample (x=0.01 ~29 uW cm-1 K-2 at 300 K, ~22 at 623 K, versus x=0 at most ~5). The pairing supports that Se doping's effect on the band edges is consistent with, and offered as the explanation for, the step-up in PF from undoped to doped.
limits
  • The DFT panels (F2c vs F2d) contrast only undoped and Se-doped band structures; they do not resolve different Se fractions x=0.005 vs x=0.01, so the pair cannot explain why x=0.01 is highest while x=0.005 is the lowest of the doped samples
  • DFT band positions are a zero-temperature electronic-structure calculation while the power factor is a transport coefficient measured across 300-623 K, so the two are different kinds of quantity and no temperature-resolved mechanism is established
  • The combination shows the band picture is consistent with enhanced PF upon doping but does not quantify how much of the PF gain is attributable to the multi-valley convergence itself versus other transport factors (mobility, scattering) not covered by either panel
not identifiablecarrier concentration increase from Se donor electrons versus band (valley) convergence at E_F as the driver of the power factor enhancement -- both occur together with Se doping and the cited evidence does not separate their individual contributions

journal_of_m_spi_o4_o6_n9-n10
step 1 · ATOM:DFT
With Se (panel d vs c), conduction-band minima at M, K and L drop from ~0.15 eV above E_F to E_F; Gamma CB stays ~0.35-0.4 eV up
step 2 · TRANSPORT:Hall

the question, as the solver sees itDoes the upstream evidence account for the downstream observation about MEC/pathway / PRP/descriptor? Say what the combination supports and what it leaves open.
generator spine_edgedepth 2lane FMdependency realinference follows, weaklycausal strength conditional mechanism
key — the combining proposition
Together, the DFT band-structure calculation and the Hall measurement support a mechanistic account: Se substitution donates electrons that raise E_F until the M, K and L conduction-band minima (initially ~0.15 eV above E_F) reach E_F while the Gamma minimum stays ~0.35-0.4 eV higher, and this band-edge alignment is consistent with the measured rise in Hall carrier concentration from ~0.5e19 (x=0) to 1.7, 2.5, 2.9, 3.3e19 cm-3 (x=0.005-0.04) at 300 K -- i.e., Se acts as an n-type donor whose effect on the electronic structure plausibly underlies the observed increase in carrier density with x.
limits
  • The DFT comparison (F2c vs F2d) appears to be a two-state snapshot (undoped vs one Se-doped case), while the Hall data (F4a) span five x values (0, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04); the pairing cannot establish a quantitative, point-by-point correspondence between band-edge position and n_H across the full doping series, only a qualitative directional match.
  • DFT gives a 0 K electronic-structure energy level (eV relative to E_F); Hall gives a 300 K measured carrier density (cm^-3); the two are different kinds of quantity connected only through band theory, not through a shared measurement or a direct calculation of n_H from the DFT bands.
  • The combination does not rule out other contributions to the Hall-measured carrier density (e.g., temperature-dependent scattering or additional defect states) beyond the M/K/L band-edge alignment shown in the DFT panels.
not identifiableWhether the rise in n_H is driven mainly by simple additive electron doping (each Se atom donating carriers, counted rigidly) or by the multi-valley degeneracy enabled once the M, K, L minima reach E_F (more available valleys/states per donated electron) cannot be separated from this pair, since Hall measurement reports only total carrier concentration and does not resolve valley occupation.

key — the combining proposition
Across the Se-doping series, Hall carrier concentration n_H rises monotonically with x (from ~0.5e19 at x=0 up to 1.7-3.3e19 cm-3 for x=0.005-0.04 at 300 K) while resistivity falls sharply over the same series (from ~650 to 12-23 micro-ohm m at 300 K), so the two panels together support an inverse association between carrier concentration and resistivity consistent with doping-induced carrier addition lowering resistivity, and the doped samples' resistivity rising with T (metallic-like) versus x=0 falling with T is consistent with the doped samples being carrier-dominated conductors.
limits

  • resistivity depends on both carrier concentration and mobility (rho ~ 1/(n*e*mu)); mobility is not reported in either panel, so the magnitude and non-monotonic shape of the resistivity drop cannot be attributed to carrier concentration alone
  • only 4-5 doping points are given, too few to establish a quantitative relationship (e.g., a power law) between n_H and rho, only a qualitative co-trend
  • the T-dependence contrast (doped rho rising with T, x=0 falling) is a separate observation not decomposed into a carrier-concentration versus mobility contribution

key — the combining proposition

key — the combining proposition
Together, the two Hall observations show that increasing Se content (x=0.005-0.04) raises the 300 K carrier concentration n_H from ~0.5e19 up to 3.3e19 cm-3, and that over this same doping range the 300 K Hall mobility mu_H (~125-170 cm2/Vs) stays above every literature value reported at comparable n_H. Combined, this supports that Se doping adds electron carriers (consistent with Se acting as a donor) while the samples retain a mobility advantage relative to reference materials at similar carrier concentration -- i.e., the added carriers are not accompanied by a mobility penalty relative to other reported samples.
limits
  • The pairing does not establish the microscopic doping mechanism (Se substituting on the Sb site) -- that requires structural/site evidence, not just the n_H and mu_H trends across x
  • The mobility comparison is against a heterogeneous set of literature samples (different synthesis routes, microstructures, grain sizes), so the observed mu_H advantage at matched n_H could reflect differences in sample quality/scattering sources rather than being attributable solely to the Se-doping process
  • Observation B only reports mu_H behavior for the ranges x=0.005-0.02 and x=0.04, so a single optimal composition (e.g., a peak mobility at one specific x) cannot be pinned down from these two observations alone
  • The data given are a few doping points/ranges, not a dense series, so they support an ordering/trend across x but not a fitted continuous n_H-mu_H relationship
not identifiableWhether the mobility advantage over literature at matched n_H arises from reduced ionized-impurity/donor-related scattering intrinsic to the Se-doping process, versus differences in extrinsic microstructural quality (grain boundaries, secondary phases, purity) between this study's samples and the literature samples, cannot be separated using only the n_H and mu_H trends in Observations A and B.

key — the combining proposition
Observation A's temperature-dependence pattern for Se-doped mu_H (falling along T^-0.5 to T^-1 guide lines, steepening to ~T^-1.5 above ~525 K, contrasted with the x=0 sample rising with T) identifies a phonon-type scattering regime governing transport in the Se-doped samples. Observation B shows that at 300 K, the same Se-doped samples (x=0.005-0.02 at ~145-170 cm2/Vs, x=0.04 at ~125 cm2/Vs) exceed every literature mu_H value (max ~139) at comparable carrier density n_H, so the density-matched comparison indicates the advantage is not merely a carrier-concentration artifact. Together, the two panels support that the elevated 300 K Se-doped mobility relative to literature is linked to the scattering behavior captured by the T-dependence in A, i.e., an intrinsic transport-mechanism basis for the 300 K advantage rather than a density-driven one.
limits
  • Observation A alone does not pin down which scattering mechanism operates specifically at 300 K versus in the higher-T (>525 K) regime; the T^-1.5 behavior lies outside the 300 K window used in B
  • Observation B's literature comparison is against different samples/sources with unknown synthesis, purity, or grain-boundary characteristics, so an intrinsic-mechanism explanation cannot rule out extrinsic sample-quality differences as a contributor to exceeding the literature max
  • The pair does not establish why x=0.005-0.02 gives a higher advantage than x=0.04, or why any particular composition would be optimal, since B only reports a range and a single higher-x point rather than a resolved composition dependence
  • Too few points across composition to support a smooth relationship between doping level and the mobility advantage, only an ordering (low-x range and x=0.04 both exceed literature, low-x range higher)
not identifiableWhether the 300 K mobility advantage over literature (Observation B) arises from the intrinsic scattering regime identified by the T-dependence (Observation A) versus extrinsic sample-quality differences (purity, grain boundaries) relative to the literature samples cannot be separated using A and B alone

key — the combining proposition
Read together, the two panels show that at low Se doping the same samples display both anomalously high 300 K Hall mobility (mu_H ~145-170 cm2/Vs at x=0.005-0.02, still ~125 cm2/Vs at x=0.04, all above the literature envelope, with the x=0.04 case explicitly compared at similar n_H) and a large drop in 300 K resistivity (from ~650 down to ~12-23 micro-ohm m), so the two transport signatures move together in the same doping range and point to the same qualitative outcome: Se doping produces low-resistivity material with enhanced carrier mobility rather than one at the expense of the other.
limits
  • Resistivity is set jointly by carrier density n_H and mobility mu_H (rho ~ 1/(n_H*mu_H)); only the x=0.04 point is stated as compared 'at similar n_H', so for the other doping levels the resistivity drop cannot be attributed to the mobility rise alone versus a concurrent change in carrier density from doping
  • The observations are reported at only a few discrete x values (0, 0.005-0.02 lumped, 0.04), which supports an ordering/ranking across doping but not a continuous or quantitative dose-response relationship
  • The opposite temperature trends (doped rho rises with T, x=0 falls with T) show the two regimes differ in scattering/degeneracy behavior but this contrast is not used to isolate which factor (mobility or carrier density) drives the 300 K resistivity drop
  • Both readings are confined to 300 K comparisons against literature/undoped reference points; neither establishes a mechanism, only a co-occurring pattern

key — the combining proposition
In the Se-containing cell, the M, K and L conduction-band valleys sit at E_F (within ~0.05 eV) while the Gamma conduction-band minimum remains ~0.35-0.4 eV higher; this is the same DFT finding described twice, once (Observation A) as a shift from ~0.15 eV above E_F (host, panel c) to E_F (Se cell, panel d), and once (Observation B) as the resulting energetics of panel d alone. Together they say only that, for this one Se-doped structure, the M/K/L valleys and Gamma minimum sit at those two distinct energies relative to E_F -- they do not establish that this valley/Gamma spacing moves across a series of compositions.
limits
  • Only one comparison point exists (host cell, panel c, vs Se-containing cell, panel d); there is no multi-point series over which a trend or co-movement of the M/K/L level and the Gamma level can be tracked
  • Observation B is drawn from the same panel (F2d) as the second half of Observation A, so it is not an independent replication -- it restates rather than corroborates across a different condition
  • Both values are static DFT band-energy positions relative to E_F for a single modeled structure, not measurements across a doping or composition series, so 'does it move with' cannot be answered beyond this one pair of states (host vs Se-doped)

propositionholdsObservation A: 'With Se (panel d vs c), conduction-band minima at M, K and L drop from ~0.15 eV above E_F to E_F; Gamma CB stays ~0.35-0.4 eV up' and Observation B: 'In the Se-containing cell, conduction-band valleys at M, K and L lie at E_F (within ~0.05 eV); the Gamma CB minimum sits ~0.35-0.4 eV higher.'
